ordered_diagnoses: Multiple System Atrophy with Cerebellar Ataxia

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Unable to stop palatal myoclonus with voluntary muscle use
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI

raw.champion: Multiple System Atrophy with Cerebellar Ataxia
raw.rationale: The combination of progressive ataxia, autonomic dysfunction (implied by severe atrophy), and palatal myoclonus, along with the absence of genetic markers for spinocerebellar ataxia, supports this diagnosis. The presence of bradykinesia and mild rigidity also aligns with the parkinsonian features that can be seen in MSA.

rejected.label: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
rejected.why: Lack of prominent supranuclear vertical gaze palsy

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: No mention of alien limb syndrome or significant asymmetric motor features

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 7
rejected.why: Normal genetic testing for this condition

rejected.label: Dystonia
rejected.why: While palatal myoclonus could be considered a form of dystonia, the broader neurological picture including ataxia, bradykinesia, and severe atrophy suggests a more complex disorder like MSA
